items.found: The entry's notes say no regulator had approved an OTOF gene therapy when the record was written on 2026-10-16, and that an approval is what would move it to in clinical use. The European regulator accepted the same therapy's application for accelerated review later in 2026, with no decision yet. Nothing new happened in the window itself.

items.upgrade_name: A prosthetic limb fixed to the bone with nerve control

items.found: On 2026-09-17 Integrum announced that the first patient in the United States had received its e-OPRA system (a bone anchor with implanted muscle and nerve electrodes) at Northwestern Memorial Hospital, in a study led by the Shirley Ryan AbilityLab under an FDA investigational device exemption, eight patients in all, expected to conclude in 2030. That is the combination this entry's next rung is about, but an investigational exemption permits a study, not sale, so no stage moves; the entry stays at first human until a regulator approves the anchor-plus-electrodes combination.
